messages:
alex: Heads-up — since the NAT gateway swap in ap-southeast-1 ~45m ago we started seeing intermittent 502s from the edge ALB to svc-edge pods. ALB target health shows 'unhealthy (connection timeout)'.

jamie: Any recent SG/NACL changes rolled with the NAT swap?

alex: Not on SGs for the nodepool. We did replace the NAT gateway and attached a new EIP, plus a small route-table tweak for the edge subnet. I ran tcpdump on a node and saw healthcheck SYNs from the ALB IPs reaching the node, but replies never make it back to ALB. Suspect SNAT/misroute or NACL stateful mismatch.

priya: Can you paste the healthcheck IPs and the NACL rules for the edge subnet? I can check deny logs.

alex: Healthcheck CIDRs from ALB: 52.203.11.0/24, 52.204.22.0/24 (example). NACLs for subnet (egress/ingress order):

```
100 ALLOW TCP 80 0.0.0.0/0
110 ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0
130 DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0
```

That looked fine at first glance but NACLs are stateless so ephemeral reply ports need explicit allow. I don't see ephemeral range allowed.

chloe: Yup — our previous template relied on SG statefulness to permit ephemeral replies, but because ALB -> node healthchecks originate from external IPs and the NACL is blocking high ports on egress, the SYN/ACK path is getting dropped. NACL implicit DENY at 130 is catching it.

jamie: Are we running ALB healthcheck to nodeport (hostPort) or target group to pod IPs? If healthchecks go to pod IPs on host networking vs nodePort it changes who replies.

alex: It's target=instance (node) with hostPort mapping. ALB hits node:3001 which forwards to pod. Node sends reply but SNATing from nodes to internet might use the NAT gateway — after swap the NAT's security policy is default but the NACL on the subnet is stricter. I captured a single flow:

```
ALB(52.203.11.12):TCP:80 -> node(10.0.12.45):3001 SYN
node replies: node(10.0.12.45):3001 -> ALB(52.203.11.12):49152 SYN/ACK
NACL logs: egress DENY on port 49152
```

priya: That matches. Quick mitigation — add explicit ephemeral port allowance in the subnet NACL egress: 1024-65535 TCP to 0.0.0.0/0. Or narrower to ALB CIDRs if you want least privilege.

chloe: I can apply a scoped fix: egress ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 for the ALB CIDRs only, priority 120. That keeps default DENY in place for everything else.

alex: Thanks — please spike that. Also note this only affects cross-AZ ALB healthchecks that originate outside VPC. Internal ALBs that originate from VPC don't hit this path.

jamie: For long-term: we should update our infra template so NACLs for edge subnets include ephemeral egress by default, and add a test in the infra pipeline that simulates ALB healthcheck flows after NAT changes. Maybe a k8s job that curls the hostPort via the external ALB IPs?

priya: Agreed. Also adding an automated NACL denylog alert to the SRE dashboard for ephemeral ports would have flagged this immediately. I'll add that to the runbook.

chloe: Patch applied (allowed ephemeral TCP to ALB CIDRs) — healthchecks recovered within 30s. Marking for rollback review after patch window. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: deploybot: Change applied by chloe to acl-edge-subnet (egress rule 120). Change id: dbc-2021-9981.

alex: Confirmed 200s of green health. Going to run a quick sweep for other subnets that had NAT swaps this week.

jamie: For the follow-up ticket, include: exact NACL rule diff, which NAT swaps touched which subnets, a test script to validate ALB->node reply paths, and a proposed default NACL template.

priya: I'll file the ticket and assign to eng-infra with priority P2.

alex: Thanks all. Main takeaway: when swapping NATs, check stateless NACLs for ephemeral egress — SGs won't save you for ALB-originated healthchecks. :sweat_smile:
